text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press on Saturday.

- The government worked out three anti-inflationary plans for 1998 and the programme targeting 13 percent inflation for next year seems to be the most realistic, Finance Ministry secretary of state Laszlo Akar told journalists.

- Internal conflicts within the Socialist Party (MSZP), the senior member of the ruling coalition, have made the government's job difficult, a document approved by the MSZP's presidency ahead of the June party congress said.

- State subsidies to the agricultural sector are likely to total 227 billion forints in 1998, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said at the meeting of the National Agricultural Round Table, a forum of agricultural experts and politicians.
- The number of environmental damages in the country is estimated at betwen 20,000 and 30,000.
- The Corinthia group, operating in Turkey, Tunesia and Malta bought Budapest's Royal hotel for almost 1.2 billion forints.
- The number of mandates in the Parliament should be reduced, Prime Minister Gyula Horn told an open forum.

- The latest round of talks between Hungary and Slovakia about setting up joint committees to supervise the fulfilment of obligations in a basic treaty between the countries, were unsuccessful as Slovakia refused to include the representatives of ethnic Hungarians into a committee.
